doc.title: JJ Johnson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Desert island albums
summary: His choices include Daphnis and Chloe, The Rite of Spring and Miles Ahead.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Listening to classical music, then and now

blocks.x: [David,] would you like to take us to the desert island?

Yes. If you were going to a desert island – and this is a favorite question of everybody – and you could only take five – I’m going to be really liberal. Instead of five records, [you can take] five albums. You can take five albums with you, and you have to live with them for the rest of your existence. What five albums would you take? I know that’s a hard one, and I’m hoping that it's not one where you get a chance to prepare [your list]. You’ve got to make it off the top of your head.

That is a tough one. I know two or three, but five is tough. Ravel’s Daphnis and Chloe would certainly be one. Stravinsky’s Rite of Spring or Firebird Suite would be one. Miles Ahead would certainly be one. I’d have to think about the rest. Now it's getting tough. It's getting tough now because there are so many – I have so many now that I need, you need to give me about fifteen, twenty more choices. I don’t have them. I only have two or three more choices. So it's tough. It's tough now because I can think of a few, and that exceeds your limit.
